# gh-1059 AC4: the real-keychain runner guard — `security`
      # add/find/delete against the runner's login keychain through the
      # bounded-helper machinery (outcome classification incl. stderr
      # tails, env merge, timeout kill). The group is tagged `integration`
      # (real side effects), so the Linux core shards and the pre-commit
      # gate skip it; this macOS leg is where it actually executes. Skips
      # with a named reason when no `security` binary / default keychain.
      - name: dart test secure key store (macOS Keychain live legs)
        run: dart test test/secrets/secure_key_store_test.dart --tags integration

  static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1538: the publish dry-run below rehearses the tag-stamped
          # stage (gh-1522), moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — tag math needs the full tag graph
          # (blobless per gh-1477, same incantation that leg used).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1479 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1479 - **Title**: gh-1476 [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1476` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 15 - **Additions**: +2592 - **Deletions**: -181 - **Created**: 2026-10-10T08:04:57Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-12T13:54:06Z ## PR Description Closes #1476 ### What changed fa1.dev becomes agent-legible end to end (gh-1476): a new deterministic build step (`scripts/build_site.dart` + minimal `scripts/site_markdown.dart`, pure Dart no deps) pre-renders every blog post and 5 curated docs pages to static no-JS HTML with per-page JSON-LD, regenerates `sitemap.xml` and `llms-full.txt`, and server-renders the blog index — all committed as artifacts and CI-gated against drift. ### Key decisions - **Deterministic lastmod**: front-matter `updated:`/`date:` for posts, an `updated` field in the docs registry, a registry table for static pages — no git/mtime, so CI checkouts rebuild byte-identically (this is what makes the staleness gate sound). - **One `@graph`** on the landing page: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareApplication (`sameAs` → GitHub + pub.dev) + SoftwareSourceCode (`codeRepository`, `runtimePlatform: Dart`) + the existing FAQPage/HowTo content preserved verbatim. - **robots.txt** names 11 AI crawlers with `Allow: /` and points at llms.txt / llms-full.txt; `User-agent: *` + sitemap line kept. - **llms-full.txt** (87 KB, under the 150 KB budget, builder-enforced) = llms.txt verbatim + every post and doc in full, each section headed by its canonical URL; llms.txt extended with Blog/Docs sections. - Blog body markdown stays single-source (site/blog/posts/*.md); HTML is generated, cover/H1 lifted into the template (`post.html` parity); legacy `post.html` still serves old links. - CI: `static` job runs `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check` (fails on any hand-edit/stale artifact); pages.yml rebuilds the layer at deploy and now triggers on `blog/**` + `docs/**` changes. ### How to verify ```bash dart scripts/build_site.dart --check # freshness gate (also in CI static job) dart test test/site/ test/scripts/ # 96 tests: no-JS crawl over loopback HTTP, # robots contract, sitemap integrity, # JSON-LD validation, builder units ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD MD[blog/posts/*.md + docs/*.md] --> B[scripts/build_site.dart] REG[date registries
front-matter / updated / static table] --> B B --> BP[/blog/slug/ index.html
BlogPosting JSON-LD/] B --> DP[/docs/slug/ index.html
TechArticle JSON-LD/] B --> SM[sitemap.xml
real lastmod] B --> LF[llms-full.txt
≤150 KB budget] B --> BI[blog index post list
generated markers block] CI[CI static gate
--check byte-diff] -.fails on drift.-> B PGH[pages.yml deploy] --> B ```

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag. (#1431): the SDK pin must be an EXACT
          # 3.47.x patch (no wildcard) — a floating patch re-resolves a new
          # engine build and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the
          # size gates track.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -Eq "flutter-version: '3\.47\.[0-9]+'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity + #1431 exact-patch rule, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.
      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)
        run: |
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          # The builder's post input is the site/blog/posts COPY of the
          # canonical blog/posts — keep them pinned together so the gate
          # can never validate a stale or hand-edited copy (gh-1476
          # review). PRE-sync diff: an in-place edit of the copy is red
          # (the deploy's build_blog would silently discard it). Sync,
          # then POST-sync diff: a new or edited canonical post that was
          # never copied into site/blog/posts is red.
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out "$d/site"
          FA_SITE_ROOT="$d/site" dart test/site/

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: LLM tag boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2)
        run: python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py

      # gh-1199 AC6/E3: the flake quarantine list itself must stay
      # honest — every entry documented (issue, since, >=2 proving runs)
      # and pointing at an existing integration-tagged file.
      - name: Flake quarantine list guard (gh-1199 AC6)
        run: python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check

      # gh-1296 NG1/AC2: every lockfile in the repo is committed and
      # enforced — ONE inventory list (scripts/check_lockfiles.sh) fails the
      # PR when a listed lockfile is missing, untracked, or gitignored, and
      # the guard's own red exits are fixture-self-tested so the check
      # cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Lockfile inventory gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh inventory

      # gh-1522 AC5: committed pubspecs carry the FIXED 0.0.0-dev
      # placeholder — the git tag is the single source of truth and CI
      # stamps the staged publish tree from it. A hand-bumped version in
      # either pubspec is a mistake now: it desyncs the tag↔staged-file
      # invariant the publish stamper relies on (and reintroduces the
      # lockfile churn gh-1522 retires). Runs on every PR — a bump attempt
      # is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: Version placeholder guard (gh-1522)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for f in pubspec.yaml flutter_app/pubspec.yaml; do
            v=$(grep '^version:' "$f" | awk '{print $2}')
            base="${v%%+*}"

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

blocks.text:
uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag. (#1431): the SDK pin must be an EXACT
          # 3.47.x patch (no wildcard) — a floating patch re-resolves a new
          # engine build and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the
          # size gates track.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -Eq "flutter-version: '3\.47\.[0-9]+'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity + #1431 exact-patch rule, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)

name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)

                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
